column1: # Example mutant batch for scripts/mutate.sh.
#   scripts/mutate.sh batch scripts/mutants/example.tsv
# Tab-separated: NAME <TAB> FILE <TAB> FROM <TAB> TO [<TAB> TEST_FILTER]
# FROM must occur EXACTLY ONCE in FILE or the mutant is refused.
# 🔴 This file holds MUTANT DEFINITIONS, never results. Results go in a PR
# body or a session log, stamped with the commit they describe, because a
# verdict is void the moment the tree moves.
# 🔴 TEST_FILTER is an optimisation, not a default: the full suite is ~12 min
# and these pure-JVM classes are seconds. A filter is safe here only because
# the harness refuses a run that executed zero tests — without that guard a
# typo'd filter reads as SURVIVED. Omit the column to run everything.
# Every mutant below changes ONE expression and leaves the branch structure
# intact, so a kill is attributable to that expression and nothing else.
# m1 is deliberately a SAME-LENGTH edit (20_000.0 -> 21_000.0, 8 bytes each)
# applied immediately after the previous run. That is the shape that defeats
# an mtime+size cache — the stale-.pyc trap. It is in the batch so the harness
# keeps measuring whether Gradle's input hashing really is content-based here.
m1-readtimeout-floor-samelength
m2-budget-floor-off-by-one
m3-permanent-503-marker
